findings.title: Make ownership information survive the whole journey.
paragraphs: A value that is already available should not need another continuation, boxed tuple or reference-count wrapper simply to reach its next consumer. The native backend now carries scalar, product and ownership facts through calls, loop backedges and suspension. Borrowed observers traverse shared data while an owning adapter keeps the roots alive; known unshared constructors can transfer their fields directly.

These connections made generated native code competitive. In Phase 73’s paired twelve-family campaign, average execution time fell from 1.369× to 1.051× upstream C. The list pipeline and BST matched upstream allocation counts, while Tape’s combined borrowing and storage changes reduced execution time from 896.5 to 266.5 ms. Earlier Phase 72 connected existing product transport with just 13 added physical lines.

findings.title: Stop recomputing what the compiler already knows.
paragraphs: Annotation had already computed normalized types and constructor-field quantities. Reusing those facts avoids rebuilding environments and layouts. A whole-program escape index also lets exactly saturated calls skip unneeded curried factories, shrinking the three Phase 78 timing programs’ C by 21–23%. Unsupported calls keep their ordinary path.

Phase 82 then removed fixed work from every native request. Bend prepares the invariant runtime text once; each request verifies and consumes that artifact. The request also carries its existing source-ID bound into validation, avoiding another walk. The paired campaign used 6.15% less B2 request time, with a larger 20.7% saving on the small held-out program.

findings.title: The Bend compiler can reproduce itself as a native program.
paragraphs: Moving the compiler out of a JavaScript host exposed costs that small programs had hidden: deep recursive traversals, growing-prefix String construction and repeated graph searches. Tail loops, chunk collection and indexed lookup removed those scaling barriers. Phase 90’s native compiler emitted its complete 38.6 MB C image in 164.3 seconds; the preceding version had reached a 600-second timeout without output.

Building that C exposed a different bottleneck in LLVM’s call graph. A small accessor for large dispatch tables let the optimized build finish with 3.89 GiB peak RSS after an earlier 10 GiB attempt had failed. The current candidate04 chain has a fresh exact emitted-C fixed point: native B1 and B2 reproduce all 30,373,059 bytes, with complete diagnostic agreement.

findings.title: Let efficient paths compose across ordinary source code.
paragraphs: Direct workers were available, but composing them could recreate continuations and temporary products. The new lowering keeps eligible local calls direct, turns final-field constructor recursion into loops, and recognizes owning observers whose result is immediately projected to a scalar. The resulting worker performs the borrowed computation, checks errors and releases its roots without constructing two temporary tuples.

The promoted candidate04 retains these gains with a corrected inline-cost policy. Across six source programs, native B2 uses 27.6% less request time than Phase 98. Across all 44 positive-work runtime points, generated programs use 6.3% less time and average 1.043× upstream C. All six complete application measurements improve over Phase 98, including roughly halving source-index execution time.

findings.title: The public command line is written in Bend, too.
paragraphs: Run selfhost/bend input.bend -o output.c to invoke the native compiler directly. A 152-line Bend entry owns arguments, asset identities, cache/live selection, compiler invocation, diagnostics and exit decisions. Ordinary requests need no Python, Node, Bun or TypeScript process. Three narrow C host effects provide authenticated file and byte operations.

The package locates its assets beside the executable and passes relocation, corrupt-asset refusal and atomic output-publication controls. All 41 final CLI controls pass, and six source pairs produce exactly the same C and compiler verdicts as candidate04. One small three-pair public-interface observation falls from 550 ms with the former Python launcher to 208 ms with the direct executable.

findings.title: Connect laws to the helpers being optimized.
paragraphs: The compiler now has a reusable foundation of 31 public laws independently checked by the unchanged BendTT kernel, plus executable contracts over complete production values. The suite deliberately checks incorrect implementations as well as positive examples. Independent challenges exposed two coverage gaps; the strengthened contracts cover those missing helpers without changing the original expectations.

Phase 98 connected proofs to the exact retained-string comparison, term-tag and provider-membership helpers selected for the native compiler. Thirteen distinct statements are bound to those final helper closures. A small finishing helper keeps owning Strings alive during comparison so borrowed reads can avoid per-character ownership work; paired B2 full-source requests then fell from 150.5 to 141.0 seconds.

outlook.title: Measure the whole improvement loop next.
paragraphs: The latest research audits the native stage lineage and establishes a small measurement baseline: 16 fresh requests preserve complete C and diagnostics. It does not change the installed compiler or demonstrate accelerating research yield.

Its next question is practical: does a faster compiler buy more independently validated progress? The proposed experiments compare normal and deliberately delayed compiler service, then frozen and updating builders, while charging build, validation and research costs. Smaller emitted C and cheaper Clang builds may matter as much as faster Bend requests.
